title: Diff-Aid: Inference-time Adaptive Interaction Denoising for Rectified Text-to-Image Generation
claim: Adding our plug-in module to a base generator fixes prompt-adherence and quality failures across generation, control, style and editing tasks.
layout: 4 stacked rows, 6 image columns each, baseline vs ours pairs, red prompt keywords
description: A dense four-row gallery of generated images. Each row is a different application, labeled on the left: (a) text-to-image, (b) conditional control, (c) LoRA integration, (d) instructional editing. Rows are separated by dashed lines. Every row has six square images with bold titles above them, pairing a baseline (FLUX, FLUX Canny, FLUX Depth, FLUX Sketch, FLUX Glass, FLUX Kontext) with the same model plus Ours. Input or source images (Canny edges, depth map, source portrait, gallery photo) appear in the control and editing rows. Handwritten-style captions under the images give the prompts, with key words in red, such as 'yellow stop sign', 'pink banana', 'hexagon' and 'Add a tiger'. The baselines miss those details and the Ours images match them. The eye goes first to the colorful top row and the stop sign.
caption: We present Diff-Aid to adaptively improve the interaction between textual conditions and image latents during test time. Benefited from our plug-in and interpretable design, Diff-Aid enables improved prompts following and synthesis quality for (a) text-to-image generation, (b) adding conditional input for controllable generation, (c) integrating off-the-shelf LoRAs and (d) zero-shot instructional image editing.
abstract: Recent text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models have achieved remarkable advancement, yet faithfully following complex textual descriptions remains challenging due to insufficient interactions between textual and visual features. Prior approaches enhance such interactions via architectural design or handcrafted textual condition weighting, but lack flexibility and overlook the dynamic interactions across different blocks and denoising stages. To provide a more flexible and efficient solution to this problem, we propose Diff-Aid, a lightweight inference-time method that adaptively adjusts per-token text and image interactions across transformer blocks and denoising timesteps. Beyond improving generation quality, Diff-Aid yields interpretable modulation patterns that reveal how different blocks, timesteps, and textual tokens contribute to semantic alignment during denoising. As a plug-and-play module, Diff-Aid can be seamlessly integrated into downstream applications for further improvement, including style LoRAs, controllable generation, and zero-shot editing. Experiments on strong baselines (SD 3.5 and FLUX) demonstrate consistent improvements in prompt adherence, visual quality, and human preference across various metrics. Our code and models will be released.
